rules.title: Residential rental application fee capped at $50 (CPI-adjusted)
rules.requirement: A landlord or its agent cannot charge more than $50 (adjusted yearly for inflation starting January 1, 2027) as an application or similar fee to apply to rent or sublease a home. If you were overcharged, you can report it to the Division of Consumer Affairs, and the overcharge is refunded to you out of any penalty collected.
rules.key_value: $50 per application, adjusted annually by CPI

coverage.summary: Covers residential rental units statewide, except units in one-family or two-family dwellings, and except real estate licensees who are not themselves the landlord.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Real estate licensees (New Jersey Real Estate Commission) who are not the landlord of the property

rules.exemptions: Dwelling units in one-family or two-family dwellings offered for rent; licensees of the New Jersey Real Estate Commission unless the licensee is the landlord.
rules.penalty: Up to $500 for a first offense, up to $750 for a second, and up to $1,000 for each subsequent offense, enforced under the Penalty Enforcement Law of 1999; amount wrongfully charged is remitted to the applicant from the collected penalty.
rules.quoted_span:
1. a. A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.

notes: Effective date computed from the text: act takes effect on the first day of the fourth month next following enactment; approved January 20, 2026, giving May 1, 2026. CPI adjustment of the $50 cap begins January 1, 2027 (year next following enactment). min_units set to 3 because units in one- and two-family dwellings are exempt.
